newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ex-Khmer Rouge general chides Cambodia's Hun Sen.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Khmer Rouge general chides Cambodia's Hun Sen.

text.p: A former Khmer Rouge general on Friday opposed the nomination of Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot as a replacement for ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Ei Chien, now commander of the Democratic National United Movement (DNUM) of Khmer Rouge dissidents in this western town, told Reuters the move to replace Ranariddh was inappropriate.

He also called on the international community and the United Nations to step in to help bring peace to Cambodia which has been shaken by violence in the wake of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's overthrow of Ranariddh this month.

The DNUM was formed in August last year when former Khmer Rouge foreign minister Ieng Sary broke away from the hardline, Maoist guerrilla group responsible for the "killing fields" deaths of millions of Cambodians between 1975-1979.

"We oppose the nomination of Ung Huot as it is not right. The political situation will return to normal again only if the United Nations steps in," Ei Chien said at this former Khmer Rouge western stronghold.
Ung Huot was nominated by remnants of Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party for the first prime minister's post and the idea was backed by Hun Sen.
Ei Chien also condemned Hun Sen's ouster of Ranariddh, saying that it had inflicted more harm on the country.
"Whether or not there will be an election in Cambodia depends on the U.N....without the organisation there will be no peace in Cambodia," he said.
The Cambodian government had set a general election for next May before the political turmoil set in.
The DNUM's statement comes on top of international criticism of Hun Sen for deposing Ranariddh and backing Ung Huot to take over from the prince.
The former guerrilla group, which has several thousand ex-Khmer Rouge members, is well armed and exerts considerable political influence around the gem-rich and booming western town of Pailin.

The DNUM has a stake in the domestic political situation because its leader, Ieng Sary, has said the group may take part in the next elections and its chances of winning in the area under its control look good.
